source: Defaults for regions outside Chicago, laid over data/rules/feasibility_defaults.json. Only what differs is here. A region can lay its own file over this one.

unit_size_sqft.note: starting sizes; each region's comp pool shows the local median (python -m jobs.check_region)

circulation_note: houses, duplexes and townhomes have no shared halls or stairs

production.note: NAHB Cost of Constructing a Home 2024: $428,215 average construction cost on 2,647 finished sq ft, about $162 per sq ft, from 41 builders nationwide. A national figure, not yet checked against local jobs; the range is wider for that reason. 4-6 units adds $8 per sq ft, the same step as the Chicago presets.

build_spec_presets.status: national survey figure; replace with local job costs when available

escalation.base_note: mean of the 12 monthly values of the Census under-construction index for 2024, the NAHB survey year

sprinklers_note: the International Building Code treats 3 or more units in one building as R-2 and requires sprinklers; townhouses and 1-2 unit homes fall under the residential code. Check the state's adopted code.
soft_cost_note: the NAHB construction figure already carries site work and builder-paid fees; 15% covers design, overhead and general expenses (NAHB 2024: overhead 5.7% and financing 1.5% of price, on top of construction)

impact_fees.basis: not loaded for this city: enter the fee

margins_by_stage.why_wider: the cost base is a national survey figure with no local calibration yet

property_tax.rate_note: placeholder carried from Chicago; replace with the county millage

sale_comps.pool: 1-6 unit buildings built 2014 or later; first qualified arm's-length sale after construction, or the appraisal district's market value where sale prices are not public

method.elasticity_note: price per unit moves with size: x (target sq ft / comp sq ft) ^ elasticity; each region refits it with python -m jobs.check_region --write
